walkthroughs.body_html: A poem on love may draw from a semantic field of warfare (arrows, conquest, surrender). Identifying the field is the first step in tracing its argument.
Patterns of sound do interpretive work. Sibilance can soothe or hiss; plosive consonants can punctuate or violence. Always link sound to sense.
Leech's foregrounding asks: what departure from norm grabs attention? An unusual word order, an unexpected register shift, a sudden archaism — these earn attention.

mcqs.q: What did Romantic poets value in nature?
options: Nature as a source of spiritual insight and emotional truth, accessed through imagination — not picturesque scenery for its own sake.
Romantic poets just liked to write about pretty landscapes.
Context is required because all texts are about history.
Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.

mcqs.q: What is the structure of a Shakespearean sonnet?
options: A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
A sonnet is any short love poem.
Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.
Fourteen lines in iambic pentameter, structured as three quatrains and a final couplet, rhyming ABAB CDCD EFEF GG, often with a volta near the couplet.

mcqs.q: Why does historical context matter when reading literature?
options: Context is required because all texts are about history.
Texts emerge from and respond to specific historical conditions — context illuminates references, assumptions and arguments that might otherwise be invisible.
Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.
Context just means writing about what the author had for breakfast.
